no_target_yet.statement: For every positive integer $n$, $P_n$ is primitive if and only if no prime in $\mathcal B$ divides $n$. The increasing sequence $a$ exists, begins with $a(1)=1$, and for any term $a(k)=uv$ with $u,v>1$, both $u$ and $v$ are terms of index greater than one. In particular, the factorization of any term into prime terms is unique up to order.

no_target_yet.statement: For $n\geq1$ and $r\in\mathbb Z$, $Q_{n-1}(nx+r)$ is primitive if and only if $F_{(r-1)\bmod p}\not\equiv0\pmod p$ for every prime $p\mid n$, where $(r-1)\bmod p$ denotes the least nonnegative residue. For each fixed $r$, its primitive indices are closed under products and positive divisors.
